summary: Adversarial verification of the biome traits (docs/BIOME_TRAITS.md, contract 27) as built by traits-core. I found no Core bug, so I changed no Core code. (1) Classic bit-identity holds. I built a Windows player into Build/traits-verify through the lock (Build Finished: Success) and ran the classic probe at -fps 30 and -fps 144: PASS both times, [ProbeHash] 246577239DE179C4 both times, 8 screenshots each, no exception in the player logs. In the Core: a null trait set, Parse(';;') and a set with all eight specs DISABLED and invalid parameters reproduce the pre-trait rolling hash 8CB763231AC73608. All eight traits ENABLED at neutral parameters (Inertia 540, Coalescence 0, SparkSpeed 1.8, Propagation rings 0, ScorchedEarth 15, Conduction 1, ArcReach 1, RingInterval 15) evolve exactly like classic, every tick of full 90 s bot rounds at 30, 60 and 144 Hz with the lasso on: positions, headings, trails, sparks, grid and every event with its time and cells match, so the hook plumbing has no side effect. (2) Switching one trait off has no side effect on the others. For each of the 9 traits of the 3 biome sets, the set with that trait disabled and the set without that spec give identical StateHash on every tick, and the other traits keep their parameters and config fields. Each trait alone equals the full catalogue with only that trait enabled. Inert traits leave the rest bit-identical: ScorchedEarth alone == classic; Feu minus Propagation == SparkSpeed(2.1) alone; RingInterval with the lasso off == classic, alone and inside Electricite; Coalescence(0) inside Liquide == Inertia alone. Spec order and earlier duplicates do not matter. Reflection over all 30 SimConfig fields shows that each config trait writes only its own fields and each behaviour trait writes none. (3) No trait can test the biome: grep finds biome words only in Core comments, and a reflection test finds no type, member or parameter in the Core assembly naming a biome (BiomeId lives in Runtime, which Core cannot reference). Any combination runs: all eight together, three unions of two biome sets, and six seeded random subsets with random valid parameters all keep every invariant, round-trip their key and are deterministic. (4) Every biome set (30 Hz lasso off, 60 and 144 Hz lasso on, full 90 s rounds) is deterministic (twin StateHash compared every 15 ticks), EventCapHits == 0, and passes independent oracles on every tick: exact Propagation ring cells, rebuilt from the grid as it was just before growth (Feu: 64 growth instants and 194k grown cells checked; 176 cells spared under heads, 494 by own trails, 3097 scorched); the Coalescence hole postcondition after isolated unchased returns (339 checks); spark closed form on the BASE pawn speed; Conduction and Inertia step limits; and R10 / R11 cut geometry under ArcReach (32 cuts over 12 extra full rounds, 733 spark ticks). (5) Section 2 edge cases, scripted and checked across rates: the home claimant's own head disc is spared by Propagation; an ArcReach cut at the HeadGrace boundary (head-on pass at 0.8 u) gives s_cut = L(t) - HeadGrace at exactly ContactRadius 0.882, and the classic round never cuts; config traits act on the cloned config only (every caller field, the caller's RuleTraits reference and value, later caller edits and the given TraitSpec objects stay isolated). Results: dotnet 443 / 443 green (399 existing + 44 audit cases). Unity EditMode through the lock: 605 cases, 602 passed, 2 skipped (existing), 1 failure from another package (WaveC_Composites_KeepTheirFetchCount, LiquidComposite fetch sites 14 vs 13, liq-drop F2 work in progress); all 19 audit cases of the Unity subset pass.
contract_issues: Inertia validation gap: TraitDefaults accepts Inertia P1 = 0 (P1 >= 0), but R3 and SimConfig define TurnRateDeg = 0 as INSTANT turns, the opposite of 'slower max turn rate'. No test uses Inertia(0). Proposed one-line fix (not applied, it changes what keys are accepted): mark Inertia's P1 minimum as exclusive (P1 > 0) in TraitDefaults.Rows, or state in section 27 that Inertia(0) means instant turns.

Propagation 'never triggers its owner's return' (reading, verified): the strict sense holds. The head disc (current Cell + cell centers within HeadRadius 0.45 u) covers every cell a head can enter during the next tick (the largest step is 0.26 u, at 30 Hz with Conduction 1.3). The bot-round oracle confirms that no Return in the tick after a growth enters a cell grown for that player at that instant. The loose sense does not hold: cells beyond HeadRadius in front of a trailing head can grow, so the land moves toward the head and the return comes earlier. That follows from the section 2 exclusion list; section 27 should say so.

ArcReach design note: with ContactScale 1.4 the cut radius is 0.882 u, close to HeadGrace 1.0 u. During a max-rate turn (540 deg/s at 6 u/s gives a radius of 0.637 u), the chord of the protected last 1 u of trail is about 0.90 u. An enemy head passing right over the victim's head therefore cuts with a lateral offset of only about 0.02 u toward the trail (the classic radius 0.63 leaves 0.27 u). In tight turns, 'heads pass through heads' (R10) becomes very narrow. This is a user decision (for example, scale HeadGrace with ContactScale, or keep ArcReach at or below about 1.35); no change made.
